statements.text: DEFINE changing position IS a manoeuvre THAT changes lanes OR overtakes and passes another vehicle
DEFINE passing IS a lane change THAT moves past a slower vehicle | ALSO CALLED overtaking

flags.note: The handbook uses "pass", "overtake" and "overtake and pass" for the same manoeuvre.

statements.text: FACT vehicles on the same road do not all travel at the same speed, even though every public road has a speed limit
FACT cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers preparing to turn are [?usually] slower than through traffic

flags.note: Hedged generalisation.

statements.note: "You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles" is motivation, not a permission, so no MAY rule is written for it.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD start a lane change or a pass | ONLY IF the driver has [?enough] space and time to complete it [?safely]

flags.note: No measure of space or time.
Judgment term.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle | UNLESS the driver is [?sure] the pass can be made without danger to the driver or others

flags.note: Subjective certainty; no observable test.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass | WHEN the driver is [?in doubt]

flags.note: Subjective state; the catch-all behind 2.1b.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD keep to the right of the road, or to the right-hand lane of a multi-lane road | UNLESS the driver is turning left OR passing another vehicle
TO pass a vehicle

flags.note: Called "rear view mirror" in the night procedure (3.3.1b).

statements.note: Steps 1 and 2 restate the lane-change steps on the same page; the order of the steps carries "only after signalling".

steps.text: signal left AND check that the way is clear ahead and behind
WATCH FOR bicycles and small vehicles hidden in front of the vehicle being passed, vehicles turning left ahead, and vehicles or pedestrians entering from a road or driveway
signal right to return to the original lane
move back into the original lane | WHEN the entire front of the vehicle being passed is visible in the inside mirror
IF the vehicle being passed speeds up | THEN do not race AND go back to the original lane

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut off the vehicle being passed by moving in front of it suddenly | WHEN returning to the original lane
a driver MUST NOT pass a vehicle | WHEN the driver is within 30 m of a pedestrian crossover

flags.note: Stated on two pages (Changing positions, Stopping) in different words; the meanings agree.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass [?on the left of a centreline] | WHEN the driver is [?30 m from] a bridge, viaduct or tunnel

flags.note: "30 metres from" is read as "within 30 m of"; the text does not say whether it covers both approaches.

flags.span: on the left of a centreline
flags.note: Prohibits the means (crossing the centreline), not passing as such; passing on a multi-lane road near a bridge is not covered.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass | WHEN (the driver is approaching the crest of a hill OR the driver is on a curve) | AND the view of oncoming traffic is obstructed | AND the clear distance ahead is not [?enough] to pass [?safely]

flags.note: No distance given.
Judgment term.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT use a two-way left-turn lane for passing
statements.basis: default (prescriptive passive "are not to be used")

flags.note: Not an imperative and no legal marker; the default puts it at SHOULD NOT, but the wording reads like a prohibition.

statements.text: FACT pavement markings show, among other things, where it is not [?safe] to pass

flags.note: Judgment term inside a description.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass | WHEN there is a solid line at the left of the driver's lane | BECAUSE a solid line there means it is unsafe to pass
a driver MAY pass | WHEN there is a broken line at the left of the driver's lane | ONLY IF the way is clear AND there are [?enough] broken lines ahead to complete the pass [?safely]

flags.note: No distance given.
Judgment term.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass | WHEN a "do not pass" sign applies to the road
statements.basis: context (Regulatory signs: "These signs give a direction that must be obeyed")
statements.note: The sign's own caption is a plain imperative; the legal force comes from the section introduction.

statements.text: DEFINE a passing lane or climbing lane IS an added lane THAT lets slower vehicles move into the right-hand lane so faster vehicles can pass [?safely] in the left lane

flags.note: Judgment term inside a definition.

statements.text: FACT an advance sign tells drivers a passing opportunity is coming, AND another sign warns when the added lane is ending
a driver in the right-hand lane SHOULD merge [?safely] with traffic in the left-hand lane | WHEN a sign warns that the lane is ending
statements.basis: implied ("so drivers … can begin to merge safely")

flags.note: The rule is implied by a purpose clause about the sign; the text states no instruction.
Judgment term.

statements.text: a driver MUST keep to the right lane | WHEN a "keep right except to pass" sign is posted | UNLESS the driver is passing on a two-lane section where a climbing or passing lane is provided
a driver on a freeway SHOULD keep to the right AND use the left lanes for passing
a driver SHOULD use the far-left lane of a multi-lane freeway | ONLY IF the driver is passing traffic that moves slower than the speed limit
statements.note: "Use the far left lane … to pass …, but don't stay there" is read as: that lane is for passing only.

statements.text: a driver on a freeway SHOULD drive in the right-hand lane | WHEN [?possible] | BECAUSE this leaves the other lanes clear for passing
statements.basis: imperative ("Drive in the right-hand lane", "Get into the habit")

flags.note: No test for when it is possible.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass on the left | BECAUSE passing on the right can be more dangerous
statements.basis: default (stated as a description: "Most passing is done on the left")

flags.note: The default is described, not instructed; it is needed so that 3.2.3b reads as an exception.
Hedged generalisation in the source.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO 3.2.3a: a driver MAY pass on the right | WHEN the road is multi-lane OR the road is one-way OR the vehicle being passed is a streetcar OR the vehicle being passed is turning left
a driver SHOULD wait | WHEN the driver is in the leftmost lane with a slower vehicle in front | UNTIL the slower vehicle moves to the right
a driver SHOULD NOT change lanes suddenly to pass on the right | WHEN the driver is in the leftmost lane behind a slower vehicle | BECAUSE the driver in front may move to the right at the same time
a driver MAY drive on the right shoulder | ONLY IF the driver is passing a vehicle that is turning left AND the shoulder is paved

flags.note: Presupposes that driving on the shoulder is otherwise not allowed; that default is not stated here.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass on the left shoulder, whether or not it is paved
a driver SHOULD pass with [?extra care] | WHEN it is night

flags.note: A caution with no named hazard, so WATCH FOR does not fit.

statements.text: TO pass a vehicle at night | SPECIALIZES 2.2a | WHEN the driver has to pass AND the way is clear

flags.note: The same check is "inside mirror" in 2.2a.

steps.text: switch to low beams | WHILE approaching the vehicle from behind
signal, check the mirrors and blind spot, AND pull out to pass
switch on high beams | WHILE alongside the vehicle being passed | BECAUSE this shows more of the road ahead
pull back into the right lane AND signal | WHEN all of the front of the vehicle being passed is visible in the rear-view mirror

statements.text: a driver SHOULD use low beams | WHEN the driver is less than 60 m behind another vehicle | UNLESS the driver is passing it
a driver SHOULD NOT pass | WHEN driving in fog
statements.note: The fog advice says "Avoid passing" in one list and "Don't pass" in another; both map to SHOULD NOT.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT speed up to pass a slow-moving vehicle | WHEN driving in fog
a driver SHOULD NOT pass | WHEN driving in blowing snow or a whiteout
a driver SHOULD NOT attempt to pass a slow-moving vehicle | WHEN driving in blowing snow or a whiteout
a driver SHOULD WATCH FOR doors opening suddenly AND doors opened to load or unload | WHILE passing parked vehicles
FACT motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds [?often] move to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions OR to be seen

flags.note: Hedged generalisation.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a motorcycle, bicycle, limited-speed motorcycle or moped within its lane | BECAUSE its position in the lane is not an invitation to pass (3.4.2a)
statements.basis: imperative ("Do not take this as an invitation")

statements.text: a driver SHOULD change lanes | WHEN passing a motorcycle, bicycle, limited-speed motorcycle or moped
a driver SHOULD NOT pass a [?smaller vehicle] that is turning left ahead | UNTIL it has moved to the right

flags.note: Refers back to motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds turning left at an intersection, named two sentences earlier.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pull up beside a [?smaller vehicle] that is turning left ahead to make the turn at the same time | WHEN the driver is also turning left, behind it
statements.basis: imperative ("do not pull up beside it")

flags.note: The source says "one of these vehicles": the motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds named in the sentence before.

statements.note: Pulling up beside a turning two-wheeler is the start of a pass.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stay behind a [?smaller vehicle] that is turning left ahead | WHEN the driver is also turning left, behind it | UNTIL the way is [?clear]

flags.note: Same vehicles as 3.4.3b; the source only says "Stay behind".
No test for when the way is clear.

statements.note: "… and turn when the way is clear" is written as the end of the wait (UNTIL).

statements.text: a cyclist MAY use any part of the lane | WHEN this is [?necessary for safety], for example to discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared [?safely]

flags.note: Judgment of the cyclist.
Judgment term.

statements.note: A rule for the cyclist, not the passing driver.

statements.text: a driver of a motor vehicle MUST keep at least 1 m between the vehicle and a cyclist | WHILE passing the cyclist, [?where practical] | IF VIOLATED a fine AND 2 demerit points

flags.note: Leaves open when the 1 m minimum can be set aside.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD change lanes to pass a cyclist | WHEN [?possible]

flags.note: No test for when it is possible.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT sound the horn [?unnecessarily] | WHILE overtaking a cyclist | BECAUSE it may frighten the cyclist and cause a loss of control

flags.note: Who judges necessity is not stated.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD tap the horn quickly and lightly while still [?some distance] away from the cyclist | WHEN the driver feels the horn must be used

flags.note: No distance given.

statements.text: a driver MUST pass a streetcar on the right | UNLESS the driver is on a one-way road
a driver SHOULD stay at least 2 m behind the rear doors of a streetcar | WHEN the streetcar is stopped AND passengers are getting on or off

flags.note: The diagram's alt text calls it "the required two metres", which suggests a legal requirement.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO 3.4.5b | WHEN the streetcar stop has an area set aside for passengers
a driver SHOULD pass a streetcar passenger area at a [?reasonable speed] | AND SHOULD WATCH FOR pedestrians making sudden or unexpected moves

flags.note: No speed given.
The source says "these areas"; read as the passenger areas in 3.4.5c.
Sharing the road (pedestrians) repeats it: "Pass these safety islands and zones at a reasonable speed. Always be ready, in case pedestrians make sudden or unexpected moves."

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut in [?closely] in front of a large vehicle | WHEN returning to the lane after passing it | BECAUSE this reduces the space cushion the large vehicle needs to stop [?safely]

flags.note: No gap given.
Judgment term.

statements.note: The source also calls it discourteous.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD allow [?more room] | WHEN passing a large vehicle

flags.note: Comparative with no baseline.

statements.text: FACT a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence THAT may affect the driver's control | WHILE passing it
DEFINE a long commercial vehicle IS a double-trailer vehicle THAT can be up to 40 m long AND carries an LCV placard on its rear | ALSO CALLED LCV
a driver SHOULD anticipate the extended length AND limited speed of an LCV | WHEN preparing to pass it
a driver SHOULD stay [?well back] of farm machinery | AND SHOULD NOT pass it | UNTIL it is [?safe] to do so

flags.note: No distance given.
Judgment term.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD keep a [?safe] following distance behind a horse-drawn vehicle | AND SHOULD NOT pass it | UNLESS it is [?safe] to do so

flags.note: Judgment term (twice).

statements.text: a driver SHOULD leave [?as much distance as possible] | WHILE passing a horse-drawn vehicle | BECAUSE passing too closely could startle the horse and make it change direction suddenly

flags.note: No distance given.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a snow plow | WHEN the snow plow is moving

flags.note: Absolute wording ("under any conditions") without a legal marker; the default gives SHOULD NOT.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass between snow plows | WHEN several snow plows are staggered across a freeway | BECAUSE there is not [?enough] room to pass [?safely] AND the ridge of wet snow can throw the vehicle out of control

flags.note: Judgment term.
Judgment term.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a pilot vehicle or pace vehicle | WHEN it carries the "do not pass" temporary condition sign

flags.span: Do not pass the pilot vehicle
flags.note: Temporary condition signs are introduced as warnings, so the section gives no legal force; the wording is a direct prohibition.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle | WHEN the vehicle is stopped at a crosswalk | BECAUSE a stopped vehicle may mean a pedestrian is crossing
FACT school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have [?illegally passed] a school bus

flags.note: Implies a prohibition on passing; the law behind it is the duty to stop in 3.4.12b.

statements.note: The law behind it is 3.4.12b, from the same section of the Stopping page.

statements.text: a driver MUST stop | WHEN approaching a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, from either direction | IF VIOLATED a [?heavy] fine AND 6 demerit points for a first offence

flags.note: The handbook says "fined heavily" and gives no amount.

Sharing the road states the same law but also counts the stop arm: "When you see a school bus with its overhead red lights flashing or its stop arm activated … You must stop whether you are behind or approaching the bus". The Signs page and the six-point offence table repeat it.

statements.note: This duty to stop is what makes passing a stopped school bus illegal (3.4.12a).

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stop at least 20 m from the bus | WHEN approaching a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing from behind

flags.note: A bare imperative in the paragraph that opens with "You must stop"; it reads as part of the law in 3.4.12b, but the handbook does not say so.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT go | WHEN stopped for a school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing | UNTIL the bus moves OR the lights have stopped flashing

flags.note: A bare imperative that sets when the duty to stop in 3.4.12b ends; it reads as part of that law, but the handbook does not say so.

flags.span: and its stop arm is no longer activated
flags.note: Two other passages end the stop differently: the same page says "Remain stopped until the arm folds away and all lights stop flashing", and Sharing the road says "until the bus moves, the overhead red lights have stopped flashing and its stop arm is no longer activated". Those need every condition; this one needs either.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO 3.4.12b | WHEN the road has a median strip AND the driver is approaching the bus from the front

a driver MUST slow down AND proceed with [?caution] | WHEN approaching, in the same direction, an emergency vehicle stopped with red or red-and-blue lights flashing OR a tow truck stopped with amber lights flashing | IF VIOLATED 3 demerit points

flags.note: Judgment term.

statements.note: The offence table words it as "Failing to slow and carefully pass a stopped emergency vehicle".

statements.text: a driver MUST move into a lane away from the stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck, [?if safe to do so] | WHEN the road has 2 or more lanes in the driver's direction | IF VIOLATED 3 demerit points

flags.note: Judgment term.
The offence table qualifies the same duty with "where possible" instead of "if safe to do so".

statements.text: FACT a vehicle towing a trailer cannot accelerate as quickly AND needs more space | BECAUSE it is much longer
a driver towing a trailer SHOULD pass | ONLY IF the driver has [?enough] time and room to complete the pass

flags.note: Judgment term.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD allow [?more room] before moving back into the lane AND SHOULD NOT cut back in [?too soon] | WHEN returning to the lane after passing | BECAUSE this can make the trailer sway and become hard to control

flags.note: Comparative with no baseline.
No gap given.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD signal, pull over AND let the other vehicles pass | WHEN the driver is holding up a line of traffic

flags.span: If you are holding up a line of traffic
flags.note: Worded for any driver, but placed in the towing section; scoped here to towing.

statements.text: FACT fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them THAT can whip a trailer to the side | WHEN they pass
a driver towing a trailer SHOULD NOT brake AND SHOULD steer the vehicle and trailer [?carefully] back into position | WHEN a passing bus or truck pushes the trailer out of position

flags.note: Judgment term.

statements.note: "A slight increase in speed may help" is a possibility, not a permission, so it stays as a note.

statements.text: a driver being passed SHOULD move to the right AND let the faster vehicle pass [?in safety] | WHEN faster traffic wants to pass

flags.note: Sample test question 5 says "you must: Move to the right and allow such vehicle to pass", and the offence table lists "Failing to share the road" (2 points), which may be the law behind it; the handbook text itself only advises.
Judgment term.

statements.note: Two of its sources come from the sample test page (question 5); keep them out of the rule set if that page is used for evaluation.

statements.text: a driver being passed MUST NOT speed up | WHILE another driver is trying to pass | BECAUSE it is dangerous
a driver MUST NOT drive to prevent another vehicle from passing | IF VIOLATED [?sanctions for dangerous driving]

flags.note: The passage lists the behaviour but does not state its sanction.

statements.text: a driver in [?slow traffic] MUST keep right | WHEN on a multi-lane road where a "slower traffic keep right" sign is posted

flags.note: No speed given; slow compared with the traffic around it.

statements.note: The caption of a regulatory sign. It is the legal side of keeping right so faster traffic can pass (2.1d, 3.6.1a).

statements.text: a driver being passed SHOULD WATCH FOR oncoming traffic AND SHOULD move closer to the right side of the lane | WHEN on an undivided road AND the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane

a driver being passed SHOULD be ready to slow down | WHEN on an undivided road AND the passing driver is in the opposite lane | BECAUSE slowing down lets the passing driver get back in front sooner and prevents a collision
a truck driver MUST NOT drive in the far-left lane | WHEN on a high-speed road with 3 or more lanes in each direction where trucks are barred from that lane

flags.note: The source says this holds on "many" such roads without saying which; the condition above restates the gap rather than filling it.
The Freeway page says "many freeways"; Changing positions says "many high-speed roads".

statements.note: A rule for truck drivers. The passing rule for other drivers (3.6.3c) depends on it.

statements.text: a truck driver MUST use the lane next to the far-left lane for passing | WHEN on a high-speed road with 3 or more lanes in each direction where trucks are barred from the far-left lane
a driver in the truck passing lane SHOULD move into the right-hand lane [?as soon as the driver can] | WHEN a truck wants to pass

flags.span: as soon as the driver can
flags.note: No time given (the handbook says "as soon as you can").
